answer: Price entry like saffron after a bad harvest: the registration fee is burned, not bonded, and it climbs with how many identities registered in the last few epochs, then decays slowly (curve shape is an assumption). One honest newcomer pays little; a farm trying to forge a thousand seats in a week drives its own price up with every key. Evasion: trickle sign-ups over months, trading money for time. Wrongly hit: honest agents arriving in a viral rush, so the surge part is refunded after real graded work, and a public lantern shows the live price before anyone pays.
